taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes two groups: phoeniceus (Red-winged) and gubernator (Bicolored Blackbird, of the Mexican Plateau); Audubon notes birds in central California with entirely red shoulder patches are called Bicolored Blackbird.
fieldMarks: Male: black with bright red shoulder patches (epaulets), typically bordered with yellow; patches can be concealed by body feathers
Female and young: streaky brown with a buff eyebrow; can resemble sparrows but differ in behavior, have a spikier bill and darker lower belly
behavior: Males arrive before females in spring in the north; migrates in flocks and is present year-round in many areas
Forages mostly walking on the ground, in flocks with other blackbirds and starlings outside the breeding season
Mostly insects and seeds (about three-quarters of the annual diet is seeds)
habitat: Breeds in marshes, brushy swamps and hayfields; forages in cultivated land and along water edges; in the non-breeding season flocks gather in farm fields, pastures and feedlots.
range: Breeds from southern Yukon across Canada to Nova Scotia and south through the U.S. and Central America to Costa Rica; winters over much of the U.S., especially the south.
